gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patient must have histologically confirmed diagnosis of: WHO grade III or IV glioma or glioblastoma or gliosarcoma. This definition also includes anaplastic astrocytoma, anaplastic oligodendroglioma, and anaplastic mixed glioma.

candidate_evidence.quote: Xevinapant is an investigational medication, taken orally, that promotes cancer cell death via apoptosis.
Researchers will investigate the ability of Xevinapant to cross the blood-brain barrier and exert anti-tumor effects on rHGG through activation of apoptosis.

tumour_pk_planned_evidence.quote: Concentration of unbound Xevinapant in brain tumor tissue in an exploratory manner (within contrast enhancing tumor as well as non-enhancing tumor, wherever possible) at the time of planned salvage resection.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Researchers hypothesize that oral administration of Xevinapant has acceptable safety and tolerability in patients with recurrent HGG and demonstrate pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic effects in HGG tumors.
We will enroll at least 4-6 subjects with archival tissue for biomarker/PD studies.

role_evidence.quote: Participants will be given a course of orally administered Xevinapant at 400 mg once daily for 4 consecutive days, prior to undergoing clinically indicated tumor resection.

agents.drug_class_hint: investigational oral IAP antagonist / SMAC mimetic (Debio 1143)
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: promotes cancer cell death via apoptosis (activation of apoptosis)

coder_notes: Window-of-opportunity phase 1 with tumour tissue PK (unbound drug in resected tumour) and stated pharmacodynamic objective in tumour with archival paired tissue -> target engagement yes. No specific tumour molecular biomarker named. Eligibility uses WHO grade III/IV terminology and lists glioblastoma/gliosarcoma explicitly -> historical.
